summary: This program adds up the eggs laid by a list of chickens using `reduce`, then works out how many muffins those eggs can produce at six muffins per egg.

lines.text: `reduce` is not built into the language the way `print` is, so it has to be imported from the `functools` module before you can use it.
This starts a list where each item is a dictionary, a common way to store several records that each have the same fields.
Each dictionary pairs a chicken's name with the number of eggs she laid, so both pieces of information travel together.

lines.code: total_eggs = reduce(lambda total, chicken: total + chicken["eggs_laid"], chickens, 0)
lines.text: `reduce` collapses the whole list down to one value: it walks through the chickens, and each time it adds that chicken's `eggs_laid` to the running `total`. The final `0` is the starting total, so an empty list would correctly give zero.
Since one egg makes six muffins, multiplying the egg count by six gives the number of muffins.
The `f` before the quotes makes this an f-string, which means anything inside curly braces is replaced by the value of that variable.
